Apple last month added three MacBook models to its obsolete products list, and today updated its vintage products list to include the 21.5-inch iMac with Retina 4K display released in 2019. Here are the details.

The iMac (Retina 4K, 21.5-inch, 2019) is now listed as a vintage product worldwide.

Apple maintains vintage and obsolete products lists so they know whether older devices are still eligible for hardware repairs and parts replacement.

Apple classifies products that have been discontinued for more than five years but less than seven years as vintage. Products may be classified as obsolete once they have been discontinued for more than seven years.

Apple does not necessarily move a product to the obsolete list the moment it passes that threshold, as repair and parts availability can vary by product. That said, once a product is classified as obsolete, Apple and its authorized service providers will generally stop offering related hardware repairs, and parts will no longer be available for order.

Today, the company added the iMac (Retina 4K, 21.5-inch, 2019) to the vintage products list, meaning the product may still be eligible for hardware repairs and parts replacement, subject to availability.

In fact, if you own this iMac and have been putting off repairs, it might be wise to send it in sooner rather than later.
